theorem exists_coefficient_construction (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{max u v}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{max u v}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    Nonempty (CoefficientConstruction.{u, v} l Ω D hl (f := f))

title: Constructible exceptional coefficient construction
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $k=\overline{k_0}$, and assume $\ell\ne p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; no absolute separatedness is imposed on $X,Y$. For every finite coefficient field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ put $R_E=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=R_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$. Let $s$ range over finite stages $(E,n)$, integral stages $R_E$, rational stages $E$, and the closed stage $\Omega$. Write $\mathcal C_{T,s}=D^b_{ctf}(T,s)$ for the actual full coefficient categories: ordinary constant-ring pro-etale coefficients at finite stages, completed derived-complete coefficients with uniform finite-level Tor bounds at integral stages, raw scalar localization at rational stages, and common finite subfields of $\Omega$ at the closed stage [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. At ring stages write $I_{T,s}$ for the full inclusion into the ordinary derived category of the indicated coefficient sheaf.

There exists one family of normalized construction data, indexed by every compactification $c=(j,p_c)$ of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], with the following fields (this is exactly the record $\mathrm{WeilConjectures.ConstructibleExceptionalCoefficients.CoefficientConstruction}(\ell,\Omega,D,\ell\ne p,f)$).

(1) For each $c,s$ there are additive exact functors $F^c_s:\mathcal C_{X,s}\to\mathcal C_{Y,s}$ and $G^c_s:\mathcal C_{Y,s}\to\mathcal C_{X,s}$ and an adjunction $F^c_s\dashv G^c_s$. Both functors have coherent integer-shift structures; its unit and counit commute with shifts. For each ring stage there is a realization $r_{c,s}:I_{Y,s}F^c_s\xrightarrow{\sim}(Rp_{c,*}j_!)I_{X,s}$ with the specified coefficient sheaf [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. At finite stages $I_{X,s}G^c_s\cong(\nu_X^*f^\times_{c,s}R\nu_{Y,*})I_{Y,s}$, the fixed finite exceptional construction [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. At integral stages a second left realization identifies $F^c_{R_E}$ with the prescribed reduction-tower compact-support functor [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]; after inclusion its map is $r_{c,R_E}$ followed by the canonical ambient-to-tower realization. At rational stages $F^c_E$ is identified with the rationalization of that prescribed integral functor.

(2) An allowed ring coefficient change $a:s\to t$ is generated by finite quotients, the ramified finite maps $A_{E,n}\to A_{L,en}$ for an algebra embedding $E\to L$ of ramification index $e$, integral reduction $R_E\to A_{E,n}$, completed integral extension $R_E\to R_L$, identities with their actual identity ring maps, and composites whose actual ring-sheaf maps compose. For every such $a$ and $T=X,Y$ there is an additive exact scalar functor $T_{a,T}:\mathcal C_{T,s}\to\mathcal C_{T,t}$, with shift structure and realization $\theta_{a,T}:I_{T,t}T_{a,T}\cong S_{a,T}I_{T,s}$, where $S_{a,T}$ is ordinary derived extension along the actual coefficient-sheaf map [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For a finite target choose the literal restriction of $S_{a,T}$, so the inclusion equality is an equality of functors and $\theta$ is its equality isomorphism. For an integral extension choose the published strict-tower scalar functor itself; $\theta^{-1}$ is the canonical completed scalar comparison from ordinary derived extension to that strict-tower functor. There are scalar identity and scalar composition isomorphisms whose images under the inclusions and $\theta$ are the multiplication unitor and balanced derived tensor associator.

(3) For every $c,a$ there are invertible shift-compatible maps
$$q^c_a:T_{a,Y}F^c_s\xrightarrow{\sim}F^c_tT_{a,X},\qquad b^c_a:T_{a,X}G^c_s\xrightarrow{\sim}G^c_tT_{a,Y}.$$
The image of $q^c_a$ under the scalar and left realizations is the canonical proper/open scalar-adjunction comparison for $Rp_{c,*}j_!$. The map $b^c_a$ is its counit-normalized transpose, namely
$$\epsilon^c_{t,T_{a,Y}L}\circ F^c_t(b^c_{a,L})\circ q^c_{a,G^c_sL}=T_{a,Y}(\epsilon^c_{s,L}).$$

(4) The raw rationalization functors and rational scalar-extension functors have shift structures and individual invertible shift-compatible $q,b$ with the same counit equation. The left rationalization comparison, composed with the rational left realization of (1), is exactly the raw localization of the integral left realization. On each integral representative the rational scalar $q$ is the raw localization of the integral scalar $q$. At the common-field inclusion for every finite subfield of $\Omega$, there are such $q,b$, and $q$ is the identity on the represented compact-support object.

(5) For every proper compactification refinement $u:c\to d$ and every stage $s$ there are shift-compatible natural isomorphisms $\alpha_{u,s}:F^c_s\cong F^d_s$ and $\rho_{u,s}:G^d_s\cong G^c_s$. They satisfy both adjunction equations
$$\epsilon^d_L\circ\alpha_{u,s,G^d_sL}=\epsilon^c_L\circ F^c_s(\rho_{u,s,L}),\qquad \rho_{u,s,F^d_sK}\circ\eta^d_K=G^c_s(\alpha_{u,s,K})\circ\eta^c_K.$$
At ring stages $\alpha$ is the proper/open refinement comparison through the left realizations: use the isomorphism $j_{d!}\cong Ru_*j_{c!}$ normalized by the open unit, then its inverse and proper direct-image composition. At rational stages it is the localization of the integral refinement map. Under the common-stage $q$ it is the image of the rational refinement map. These are the fields of the construction record; identity/composition equations for the $q,b$ families and for refinements are separate coherence obligations.

The rational left functor retains the literal localized integral object and sends each localized integral arrow to the localization of the integral left arrow. The common left functor acts on every representative from index i to index j by the rational scalar comparison, the two common comparisons and the canonical transition; this is representativeAction in the construction data. These fix the action on arrows between different pair-category labels, not just arrows in a single stage inclusion. These are construction normalizations, not scalar or refinement cocycles.

proof.text: Construct ring, rational and common-stage adjunction data and the additional realization and shift normalization, without any refinement maps.
Construct only the normalized left geometric refinement isomorphisms on the same chosen operations.

For each left isomorphism take its right adjunction conjugate; the conjugation counit and unit equations and the whiskered unit/left/counit shift formula give a full RefinementComparison. Fill the refinement record from the left realization and descent formulas, then combine the four records.
